message.content: The largest planet that has been confirmed so far is **HD 100546 b**. It is a protoplanet still forming around the young star HD 100546, located about 335 light‑years away in the constellation Musca. HD 100546 b has a radius of roughly 2.5–3 times that of Jupiter (≈ 2.5–3 R_J), making it the biggest planet we have detected to date. Its mass is estimated to be a few times that of Jupiter as well, but because it is still accreting material, its exact mass is uncertain.
